strengths: Comprehensive and large-scale empirical study with 2,347 math problems, 1,196 QA problems, and 901 NL reasoning problems across 14 models and multiple domains

Novel finding that verifier generation capability exhibits difficulty-dependent non-linear correlation (saturated for easy, linear for medium, threshold-limited for hard), extending beyond prior linear characterizations
Demonstrates practical impact showing weak generators can match strong generator post-verification performance (75.5% gap reduction), with clear guidance on when strong verifiers provide no advantage
Rigorous experimental design with model-agnostic difficulty definition, careful handling of edge cases, multiple verification methods for ground truth, and analyses at multiple granularities
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and comprehensive appendices including prompt templates, case studies, and reasoning model analysis supporting reproducibility
Identifies fundamental verification limitations that verifier scaling alone cannot overcome, with important practical implications for cost-effective TTS deployment
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—primarily an empirical characterization study without new verification methods, training approaches, or theoretical frameworks; many findings are somewhat expected given prior knowledge of verification asymmetry

Restrictive scope with significant limitations: uses same model for generator and verifier (limited cross-model exploration), covers only 3 domains (math, QA, NL reasoning), excludes code generation and open-ended tasks, and only explores reference-free verification

Incomplete mechanistic understanding—case studies are illustrative but limited in depth; root causes of verification asymmetry are demonstrated but not deeply investigated; phase-transition behavior in verifier capability lacks theoretical grounding

Lacks statistical rigor—no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty quantification reported; strong claims ('bottleneck is not model capacity') lack formal statistical validation; only single 64-sample per model-problem pair

Reasoning model analysis underdeveloped—only two reasoning models examined; the finding that TNR shows different difficulty-dependence for reasoning vs. instruction-tuned models deserves deeper investigation but is relegated to appendix

Problem filtering for RQ2 excludes some problems; unclear how much data is lost and whether this introduces selection bias; experimental choices (greedy decoding, corner case handling) could affect results without sensitivity analysis

strengths: Comprehensive large-scale empirical study with 4,444 problems across 12 benchmarks and 14-15 models, providing substantial evidence
Clear stratified analysis showing difficulty-dependent correlation between verifier capability and verification performance
Practical TTS implications: demonstrates weak generators can recover 75.5% of performance gap to strong generators
Cross-domain validation across mathematics, knowledge QA, and natural language reasoning
Honest discussion of limitations and edge cases with supplementary analysis on reasoning models
Effective visualization of main findings through well-designed figures and clear presentation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily validates and incrementally refines prior findings (Chen et al. 2025c; Krumdick et al. 2025) rather than providing fundamentally new insights
Core findings are somewhat intuitive: easier problems enable better correctness recognition, weak generators produce detectable errors, verifier capability correlates with verification ability
Shallow mechanistic understanding: case studies provide post-hoc explanations but don't deeply explain why verification is harder for hard problems or why consistency matters in error detection
Limited practical actionability: findings don't clearly translate to deployment guidelines; convergence regimes occur where verification is least valuable
Experimental concerns: no significance testing, TTS formulation (Eq. 5) differs from standard practice, problem difficulty metric is relative to specific model set, arbitrary corner-case handling
Incomplete analysis of key phenomena: generator capability effects on TNR and problem difficulty effects on TPR lack quantitative depth and theoretical grounding
Scope limitations: restricted to reference-free binary-verdict verification on objective-answer domains; no analysis of computational costs despite motivation; reasoning models relegated to appendix
Reproducibility: no code link provided, potential bias from Math-Verify + LLM-as-judge fallback, no ablations on problem difficulty metric or prompt sensitivity
Missing theoretical framework: no formal model of verification difficulty or generator-verifier dynamics; verification asymmetry concept invoked but underdeveloped

strengths: Comprehensive experimental scope: 4,444+ problems across 3 domains with 14 models and GPT-4o, providing strong empirical evidence
Novel difficulty-dependent correlation regimes: Identifying nonlinear phase transitions (saturated/linear/threshold-limited) extends prior work on evaluator-generation correlations
Practical significance: Actionable findings for test-time scaling, e.g., weak generators can match strong ones post-verification (75.5% gap closure)
Rigorous methodology: Model-agnostic difficulty measure, balanced datasets, multiple analysis granularities, and proper statistical metrics
Good reproducibility: Detailed prompts, transparent methodology, robustness checks including reasoning model analysis
Generalization across domains: Findings hold across mathematical, knowledge, and NL reasoning tasks with multiple model families
Effective case studies: Figures 18-19 illuminate mechanisms (verifier error generation on hard problems, hidden inconsistencies in weak generators)
Clear practical motivation: Addresses real gap in understanding when strong vs. weak verifiers are necessary
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Purely empirical work with no new verification methods, frameworks, or theoretical tools proposed
Shallow mechanistic understanding: Documents patterns without deeply explaining why they emerge; 'solve-and-match' strategy mentioned but not systematically analyzed across failure modes
Somewhat incremental findings: Extends known verifier-capability correlation in natural directions; nonlinear regimes are novel but relatively incremental
Incomplete failure analysis: Limited systematic characterization of error detectability in strong generators; case studies are anecdotal rather than categorical
Statistical rigor gaps: Missing confidence intervals, significance tests, and uncertainty quantification on main results; no bootstrapping or formal hypothesis testing
Scope limitations: Restricted to reference-free verification, objective-answer tasks, generative verifiers, and instruction-tuned models; fine-tuned verifiers not addressed
Cross-domain variance unexplored: Why NL Reasoning shows below-random accuracy and different patterns is relegated to appendix; limited explanation of domain differences
Presentation density: Heatmaps (Figure 3) difficult to read; some redundancy between Sections 4.1 and 5.1; main paper feels like appendix summary
Limited model coverage: Models mostly in 7-72B range; missing very small (1-2B) or very large (100B+) models and other frontier models (Claude, Llama-405B)
Sensitivity analysis missing: No investigation of robustness to difficulty measure definition or generator set choice for computing d(x)

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study across 4,444 problems, 14 models, 3 domains with well-controlled experiments and proper stratification
Identifies non-linear correlation regimes (saturated/linear/threshold-limited) between verifier capability and performance that extends prior linear understanding
Strong interpretability analysis with quantitative evidence for hypothesized mechanisms (Figures 3, 5) and illuminating case studies
Practical findings demonstrating weak generators can close 75.7% performance gap with strong ones and identifying regimes where verifier scaling provides no benefit
Extensive validation across domains, reasoning models, different prompts, and large models (Qwen3-235B) demonstrating robustness
Rigorous experimental design with multiple difficulty measures (oracle and practical) and careful handling of evaluation imbalances
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual findings are somewhat intuitive (problem difficulty affects TPR, strong generators produce harder-to-detect errors, verifier capability correlates with performance); contribution is primarily systematic characterization rather than new insights

Narrow evaluation scope: limited to verifiable problems with objective ground-truth; excludes subjective reasoning, open-ended tasks, and other domains; studies only generic LLM verifiers, not trained/fine-tuned alternatives
Insufficient statistical rigor: main results lack confidence intervals and significance testing; unclear which observed differences are meaningful; no multiple comparisons corrections

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: surface-level explanations for why patterns occur; limited investigation of problem properties causing TPR degradation; missing theoretical framework for predicting regime membership

TTS application analysis incomplete: non-standard TTS metric makes comparison to related work unclear; missing direct computational cost-benefit analysis; limited guidance on transfer to other TTS strategies

Primarily descriptive rather than prescriptive: paper characterizes what happens without developing new methods, theory, or deep mechanistic insights; limited actionable guidance for practitioners beyond testing multiple verifiers

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study across 12 benchmarks, 15 models, 4,400+ problems with rigorous experimental design and clear metric definitions
Extensive supporting analysis with large-scale interpretability validation (367K+ responses) and detailed case studies providing mechanistic insights
Multi-domain coverage (mathematics, knowledge QA, NL reasoning) and thorough robustness checks (reasoning models, different prompts, larger models, alternative difficulty measures)
Well-designed methodology including balanced response sampling, oracle difficulty measure, and appropriate edge case handling with reproducible setup in appendices
Practical relevance to test-time scaling with actionable insights for model selection in deployment scenarios (Section D.2)
weaknesses: Core findings are intuitive and largely expected: (1) verifiers struggle on hard problems they cannot solve, (2) weak models produce obvious errors, (3) verification ability correlates with generation ability. These confirm intuitions rather than provide surprising insights

Limited novelty over prior work—acknowledges Chen et al. (2025c), Krumdick et al. (2025), Tan et al. (2025) found generation-verification correlation; main contribution is characterizing non-linearity, which is incremental refinement not breakthrough

Practical impact is constrained: weak generators matching strong ones requires expensive GPT-4o verifier (negating savings); weak verifiers match strong ones only at extremes where both provide minimal gains, limiting real-world utility

Purely empirical work with post-hoc interpretations (Figure 32-33) rather than theoretical explanation of mechanisms. Why does non-linearity emerge? Why does consistency in strong generators cause false positives? Lacks principled analysis

Restricted scope to verifiable problems with objective ground truth (excludes open-ended generation, code synthesis without test cases); problem difficulty is model-derived rather than inherent; largest open-source model is 72B

Methodological concern: difficulty measure uses same 64-response pool for evaluation, creating subtle dependencies; missing confidence intervals and statistical significance testing for key claims like '75.7% gap reduction'; post-hoc explanations rely on LLM-as-judge which itself may be biased

Motivation-finding mismatch: paper motivates work with 'verification asymmetry' (verification easier than generation) but Finding 3 shows verification ability closely tracks generation ability, creating apparent contradiction left unreconciled

Offers limited solutions—identifies challenges but proposes no novel verification methods to address them; recommendations are either obvious (validate on held-out set) or impractical (use expensive GPT-4o with cheap generator when GPT-4o alone might suffice)

strengths: Exceptionally comprehensive empirical study across 3 domains, 12 benchmarks, 4,444 problems, and 15 models with rigorous experimental methodology including careful sampling, multiple metrics (TPR/TNR), and extensive ablations

Rigorous mechanistic investigation beyond correlations: large-scale interpretability analysis (Figure 3: 39.1% of false negatives contain reference answer mistakes; Figure 5: surface-level error rates) explains *why* findings occur

Novel characterization of difficulty-dependent, non-linear correlation patterns: identification of three regimes (threshold-limited for hard problems, linear for medium, saturated for easy) refines prior linear assumptions

Actionable practical insights for TTS: demonstrates weak generators can close 75.7% of performance gap with strong generators; identifies computational efficiency opportunities (2.5× token savings using strong model as verifier); difficulty-stratified model selection guidance

Excellent reproducibility and transparency: complete prompt templates, detailed hyperparameters, multiple verification prompts tested for robustness, code/project links provided, extensive supplementary experiments validating core findings

Clear presentation with effective visualizations: Figure 1 provides excellent research overview; heatmaps (Figure 4) effectively communicate verifier-generator interactions; case studies illustrate mechanisms
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily confirmatory of prior correlations (Chen et al. 2025c, Tan et al. 2025); no novel verification methods or training approaches proposed; contributions are characterization rather than methodological innovation

Scope limitations reduce generalizability: restricted to verifiable tasks with objective ground truth (excludes creative/open-ended tasks); only generative verifiers studied; reasoning models show different TNR behavior suggesting findings may not generalize uniformly; no cross-task transfer analysis

Theoretical understanding gaps: no formal framework explaining why three correlation regimes emerge; identified 'solve-and-match' verification limitation explored but no solutions proposed; verification asymmetry mentioned but not deeply explored

Limited solutions to identified problems: paper identifies that verifiers struggle with hard problems and strong generators hide errors, but offers no methodological improvements—suggestions focus on practical pairing rather than advancing verification itself

Presentation issues: key practical findings (computational efficiency analysis, model selection guidance) relegated to appendix; main paper dense with complex figures; some heatmaps difficult to parse; could benefit from more concise narrative

Generalization concerns from anomalies: extended reasoning models show different TNR patterns; NL Reasoning domain exhibits below-random accuracy on hard problems (unresolved anomaly); some domain-specific variations unexplained, suggesting findings may be prompt/model-class dependent

Statistical rigor gaps: confidence intervals not shown in all figures; limited formal significance testing; some conclusions rely on trend inspection; subsampling decisions (GSM8K: 600/1,319) not analyzed for bias impact

Incomplete practical analysis: computational cost-benefit analysis of verification limited; efficiency discussed briefly in appendix (D.5) rather than main narrative; token usage analyzed in single case study, not systematically across experiments
